obligations.note: The new branch in is_allowed allows any action named 'report:<x>' whenever (role, x) is granted. These action names are not in ACTIONS and appear in no explicit grant, so unknown actions such as 'report:release_payment' are now allowed instead of denied. That breaks the explicit, default-deny matrix, which no longer equals the approved access policy. The control test only enumerates the declared ACTIONS, so it cannot detect this.

The alias only mirrors existing grants. The auditor holds no state-changing base action in GRANTS, so no 'report:' alias gives the auditor a state-changing capability. test_auditor_is_read_only passed on head.
it_admin has no approve_payment or release_payment grant, so the 'report:' aliases of those actions are also denied to it. test_it_admin_cannot_approve_or_release passed on head.

The privileged check keys on exact action names in PRIVILEGED. 'report:approve_payment' and similar names are now authorised but are not classed as privileged, which could let privileged actions run without MFA. routes.py and app.py are not in the packet, so whether any caller can reach these names cannot be established.
Ticket CHG-25503 is a standard ticket. Change manager Erik Brandt approved it at 2026-10-01T10:03Z, before the commit. Its component payments.access covers rbac.py, the only touched file.
Mara Costa is a payments change_approver and is not the author Sofia Santos. She gave a code_review approval on the head commit.
Both approvals name the head commit 6256a35, the only commit in the change.

run.json reports success on the head commit from ci-runner-04. However, the attached JUnit report is stamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-06, and its hostname is a personal machine (dev-laptop-7.local). The report cannot be reliably tied to this CI run.
rbac.py belongs to the security-sensitive component payments.access. Ines Halvorsen, a security_reviewer, gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers rbac.py. The entries cover payments.py, routes.py, audit.py and mortgage files, all unchanged, so no ledger evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds a 'report:' prefix alias to payments' is_allowed. This allows action names that are not explicitly granted and not in the action catalog, which violates the default-deny, explicitly decided access matrix required by ACC-1. It also creates a possible MFA bypass, because the aliased names are not in PRIVILEGED. Process records (ticket, independent code review, security review) are in order, but the JUnit evidence is inconsistent with the CI run record. Because ACC-1 is violated and no exception covers it, the change is rejected.
